info.title: Partner Center REST (unofficial, generated)
info.description: Generated from partner-center-mcp's verified scenario pack. Not affiliated with Microsoft.

get.summary: Verify a partner by MPN id
get.description: Omit mpnId to return the signed-in partner's profile.

Paged collection: response has totalCount, items[], and links (follow links.next for more pages).
Each item carries only companyProfile and relationshipToPartner; call get-customer-by-id for full detail.
Filter with &filter={url-encoded-json} to search by company name, domain, or reseller.
Supports both app+user and app-only.

x-variants.summary: Search customers by company name or domain

post.summary: Create a customer
post.description:
Returns 201 with a Customer that includes userCredentials (admin username/password) - save it, it cannot be retrieved later.
Idempotent: reuse the same MS-RequestId on retries to avoid creating duplicate customers.
Required body: BillingProfile (email, culture, language, companyName, defaultAddress) and CompanyProfile (domain).
A valid physical address is required; in the sandbox an invalid address makes the customer tenant undeletable.
organizationRegistrationNumber is mandatory for customers in certain countries/regions (e.g. Russia, Turkey, Brazil, India, UAE).
Do not pass a userCredentials password in the request; it is not accepted.
Also supports app-only.

get.description:
customer-id is the customer's Microsoft (Entra) tenant GUID.
Without DAP/GDAP access the response omits CompanyProfileAddress, CompanyProfileEmail, and CustomDomain.
Supports both app+user and app-only.

delete.summary: Delete a customer from the integration sandbox
delete.description:
Sandbox (TIP) only - this breaks the partner-customer relationship and purges ALL resources for that tenant.
Returns 204 No Content on success.
All Azure reservations and software purchase orders must be canceled first or the delete fails.
A customer created with an invalid sandbox address cannot be deleted.

post.summary: Create a user account for a customer
post.description:
App+User only - app-only is NOT supported. Requires a GDAP role (User Administrator or Directory Writers).
Returns 200 OK (not 201) with the created CustomerUser including its generated id.
userPrincipalName must use the customer's own (non-federated) domain.
passwordProfile.password must meet complexity rules; set forceChangePassword=true to require a reset on first sign-in.

get.summary: Get all user accounts for a customer
get.description:
App+User only - app-only is NOT supported. Requires a GDAP role (Directory Reader, Global Reader, or User Administrator).
For a single user, use /v1/customers/{customer-id}/users/{user-id}.

post.summary: Assign licenses to a user
post.description:
Returns 201 with the LicenseUpdate resource on success.
Fails if the license is not available in the customer tenant; get valid skuId values from get-subscribed-skus first.
licensesToAssign and licensesToRemove must reference SKUs from the same license group; verify the result with get-user-licenses.

get.description:
Both country and targetView are required.
targetView is an enum (Azure, AzureReservations, MicrosoftAzure, OnlineServices, Software, MarketplaceSaaS); use OnlineServices for new commerce (NCE) license-based products.
For Azure Reservations add reservationScope=AzurePlan.
403/400036 if the targetView is not allowed; 403/400030 if the targetSegment is not allowed.
Supports both app-only and app+user.

get.summary: Get a list of availabilities for a SKU
get.description:
country is required; all segments except nonprofit are returned by default (pass targetSegment=nonprofit explicitly for those).
The availability's CatalogItemId is mutable and reissued regularly - always fetch a fresh availability right before adding a cart line item or placing an order.
For Azure Reservation SKUs add reservationScope=AzurePlan; add IncludeLifeCycleState=true for NCE license-based lifecycle state.
Supports both app-only and app+user.

post.summary: Create a cart
post.description:
Carts expire 7 days after creation. Success returns 201 with the populated Cart.
lineItems is required (>=1 CartLineItem). Line items are processed in array order - place any promotion-eligible (New-To-Offer) item FIRST.
billingCycle uses snake_case JSON enum values (one_time, monthly, none).
Azure plan and perpetual software line items do NOT support termDuration - omit it for those.
Set AttestationAccepted per line item when the offer enforces attestation.
Supports both app-only and app+user.

x-variants.summary: Create a cart that includes add-ons

post.summary: Check out a cart
post.description:
Empty request body (Content-Length: 0). Success returns 201 with a CartCheckoutResult containing an orders array.
Idempotent: re-checking out an already-checked-out cart returns the original result.
Provisioning is asynchronous - subscriptionId values may be absent in the response and appear later via Get Order.
Checkout fails on an expired cart (7-day limit).
Supports both app-only and app+user.

get.description:
Use this (or list-customer-orders) to retrieve subscriptionId values not yet provisioned at checkout time.
Supports both app-only and app+user.

patch.summary: Update an order (legacy billing cycle / cancel)
patch.description:
Billing-cycle change here is for LEGACY subscriptions only; for NCE use update-subscription instead.
Out of scope: trials, monthly/Azure offers, inactive or online-services license-based subscriptions.
To cancel an order, PATCH the same path with status 'cancelled' (documented for the sandbox).

x-variants.summary: Cancel a software subscription or perpetual software purchase
Cancel an order in the integration sandbox
Purchase an add-on for an existing subscription

get.summary: Get all of a customer's orders
get.description:
There is a delay of up to 15 minutes between order submission and appearance in this collection - don't poll immediately after checkout.
Optional ?billingType={monthly|annual|one_time|none} filters by billing cycle.
Supports both app-only and app+user.

post.summary: Create an order directly (without a cart)
post.description:
For New Commerce prefer create-cart + checkout-cart: the cart validates and prices the purchase before it is placed, this route does not.
id, status, currencyCode and creationDate are read-only - they come back on the response, do not send them.
A 2xx here means the order was accepted, not provisioned: poll get-order-provisioning-status.

get.description:
Supports both app-only and app+user.
customer-tenant-id is the customer's Microsoft (Entra) tenant GUID.

x-variants.summary: Get a list of subscriptions by order

get.description:
Add-on subscriptions include parentSubscriptionId.
NCE subscriptions return extra fields (productType, termDuration, billingCycle, refundOptions, cancellationAllowedUntilDate).
Supports both app-only and app+user.

patch.description:
Send the FULL Subscription resource, not a partial patch: GET it first, mutate it, then PATCH it back.
If autoRenewEnabled or next-term instructions are set, include them in the body or they are silently reset.
Change quantity via Quantity; suspend/reactivate via Status (active/suspended); toggle renewal via AutoRenewEnabled.
Cancel an NCE subscription within its cancellation window by PATCHing Status to 'deleted' (see cancellationAllowedUntilDate).
Schedule changes for the next term (term/quantity/billing at renewal) via scheduledNextTermInstructions.
NCE license quantity can only be reduced within 7 days of purchase/renewal (else error 800090).
Billing cycle CANNOT be changed here (error 2054) - use update-order instead.
For SKU/term upgrades or trial-to-paid, use create-subscription-transition instead.
Long-running updates return 202 with a Location header to poll.

x-variants.summary: Change the seat count of a subscription
Cancel a new commerce or Marketplace subscription
Schedule changes that apply at the next term (renewal)
Change the billing frequency of a software subscription

post.summary: Migrate a legacy subscription to New Commerce (NCE)
post.description:
Only currentSubscriptionId is required; termDuration, billingCycle, purchaseFullTerm, quantity, customTermEndDate are optional and let you change terms during migration.
Omitted properties carry forward the legacy subscription's values.
Base subscriptions migrate together with all active add-ons as a bundle; if any add-on is ineligible the whole bundle fails.
addOnMigrations must be a FLAT list, not nested.
Call validate-migration first - it reports eligibility and the exact reasons this POST would otherwise fail with.
Migration is asynchronous: poll get-migration with the returned migration id, and use get-migration-events for the step-by-step trail.
To schedule rather than run immediately, use create-migration-schedule.

get.description:
size/offset are only honored for legacy invoices; for modern commercial purchases they are ignored.
Use the filter param (LeftFilter/RightFilter/Operator JSON, bounded by InvoiceDate) to avoid timeouts on large invoice sets.
Supports both app-only and app+user.

invoice-id is a string identifier, not a GUID.
App+User only (no app-only).
For modern commercial purchases this applies only to daily-rated usage and recons generated before 2025-05-15.

get.summary: Get a customer's Azure utilization records
get.description:
start_time and end_time are REQUIRED (UTC date-time offset). granularity (daily default), show_details (default true), and size (max 1000) are optional.
NOT supported for Azure plans (only legacy MS-AZR-0145P); for Azure plans use the invoice consumption line-item APIs.
If data isn't ready in billing yet, returns 204 with a Retry-After header.
Paged - follow the next link.
Supports both app-only and app+user.

get.summary: Get the partner's current account balance
get.description:
The balance is exposed via InvoiceSummary.BalanceAmount; there is no dedicated balance endpoint.
Use /v1/invoices/summaries (plural) for one summary per currency.
Supports both app-only and app+user.

post.summary: Validate an address
post.description:
Prevalidate addresses before create-customer or profile updates; the caller picks the final address from the result.
Country must be the two-character ISO alpha-2 code; required fields vary by country/region.
Only Verified or VerifiedShippable are safe to use directly; other statuses need user confirmation.

head.description:
Use the HEAD method - there is no response body; rely on the status code.
404 Not Found means the domain IS available; 200 OK means it is already in use.
The {domain} segment is the full domain string, e.g. contoso.onmicrosoft.com.

get.summary: Get a record of Partner Center activity
get.description:
Activity log data is limited to the previous 90 days; a startDate older than 90 days returns 400.
Without startDate, results default to the previous 30 days. Dates use yyyy-mm-dd.
filter must be url-encoded JSON with Field/Value/Operator (fields: CompanyName substring, CustomerId equals, ResourceType equals); matching is case-insensitive.
Results are paged.

get.summary: Get all service requests for a customer
get.description:
App+User only (no app-only).
For a single service request use GET /v1/servicerequests/{servicerequest-id}; that endpoint accepts an IncludeOrganizationRequests header for the Support Request Admin role.

get.summary: Get per-request MFA compliance for App+User API calls
get.description:
App+User only. Returns the most recent App+User API requests, capped at 10K items.
Each item exposes mfaCompliant (true/false) plus upn, objectId, applicationId, operationName - use it to find non-MFA-compliant callers before the MFA enforcement date.
This is request-level telemetry, not a static per-user enrollment record.

App+User only. Returns CustomerLicensesUsageInsights (workloadName, productName, licensesActive, licensesQualified, usagePercent).
Superseded by the workload-level GET /v1/analytics/commercial/usage/license/, but this per-customer endpoint remains documented and valid.

post.summary: Create a New Commerce transfer (billing ownership)
post.description:
The TARGET (new) partner creates the transfer; the SOURCE partner later submits it. Only Admin agents can create transfers.
transferType must be 3 (NewCommerce) - this endpoint is not for legacy subscriptions.
Customer must already have a reseller relationship with the target partner.
Returns 201 with status Pending. Common errors: 900400, 900160, 20002.

x-variants.summary: Create a transfer for legacy subscriptions

get.description:
Shows transfers from both sides - the ones this partner created as target and the ones awaiting its response as source; read status to tell them apart.
A pending transfer is the thing that blocks other lifecycle writes on the affected subscriptions; check here before diagnosing a mysterious rejection.
For one transfer's detail use get-transfer.

Either the source or target partner can read transfer status (Pending -> InProgress -> Complete).
Target partners cannot see line items until the transfer completes (new subscription/order IDs are issued then).

patch.description:
Called by the SOURCE partner; the accepting counterpart is accept-transfer, which is a POST to a different route.
Same URI as update-transfer - what differs is the status value in the body.
Rejecting leaves the subscriptions with the current partner unchanged.

x-variants.summary: Update or cancel a pending transfer

delete.description:
The only DELETE in the transfer lifecycle; accept is a POST and reject/cancel are PATCHes on the same resource.
Only the partner that created the transfer can withdraw it, and only while it is still pending.

get.description:
Partner Center has no 'reservation orders' endpoint; reservations are 'reservedinstance' entitlements, each carrying a referenceOrder.id and entitledArtifacts links.
Omit entitlementType to return all entitlement types; add showExpiry=true for expiry dates.
Reservation orders have billingCycle one_time; fetch the order itself via get-order-by-id with referenceOrder.id.
Supports both app-only and app+user.

App+User only (no app-only).
If agreementType is omitted it defaults to MicrosoftCloudAgreement; pass MicrosoftCustomerAgreement explicitly for MCA confirmations.
Agreement resource is supported only in the Microsoft public cloud (not 21Vianet or US Gov).
Returns a paged collection.

post.summary: Confirm customer acceptance of the MCA (create agreement)
post.description:
App+User only; public cloud only (not 21Vianet or US Gov). Get the templateId via Get agreement metadata first.
201 Created on success; userId is derived from the App+User token.
Re-creating with identical contact fields returns error 600061 - vary at least one field to create another.

get.summary: Get the Azure rate card (real-time prices)
get.description:
currency (ISO, default USD) and region (ISO country, default US) are optional; prices vary by market.
Response can be very large (~1.5 MB) - stream/parse efficiently.
All rates are pretax (isTaxIncluded is always false).
Use /v1/ratecards/azure-shared for Azure Partner Shared Services pricing.

eligibilityType is optional (default immediate); use the returned catalogItemId as toCatalogItemId in create-subscription-transition.
Distinct from GET .../transitions, which returns transition history rather than eligible transitions.
Empty list for trials or when eligibilityType=scheduled (you can only transition into an existing subscription via an immediate transition).

post.summary: Create a subscription transition (NCE upgrade / trial-to-paid)
post.description:
Two-step: GET transitionEligibilities first to get a valid toCatalogItemId, then POST.
Used to upgrade an NCE subscription to a target SKU/term and to convert an NCE trial to paid.
transition_with_license_transfer needs Directory Writer (GDAP); provisioning is asynchronous (response has an Events array).

get.summary: Get the transition history of a subscription (NCE)
get.description:
Returns transition HISTORY and status, not eligibility - eligibility comes from transitionEligibilities (get-subscription-transition-eligibilities).
Poll this after create-subscription-transition to see whether the transition completed; the optional operation-id query narrows it to one transition.
Distinct from the legacy /upgrades route (get-subscription-upgrades).

post.summary: Upgrade a customer to the Azure plan
post.description:
Global /v1/productupgrades collection (not subscription-scoped); the customer is identified in the body.
Returns 202 Accepted with an empty body and a Location header (productUpgrades/{id}) to poll; app+user only.
Check eligibility first via POST /v1/productUpgrades/eligibility. After upgrade, Get Subscriptions returns only the Azure plan.

get.summary: Get invoice billed reconciliation line items
get.description:
billing-provider: OneTime (modern), or Azure/Office (legacy). invoice-line-item-type: BillingLineItems or UsageLineItems.
OneTime pages via seekOperation=Next + the MS-ContinuationToken header (from links.next); Azure/Office use size+offset. Default/max size 2000.
This v1 API is in feature freeze; for new-commerce billed recon after 2025-04-21 use the async Graph v2 API.

Literal path /invoices/unbilled/lineitems (no invoice-id). Required query: provider, invoicelineitemtype, currencycode, period (current|previous).
Pages via size (max 2000) + seekOperation=Next with MS-ContinuationToken; allow up to 24h for unbilled data.
This v1 NCE API is deprecated effective 2026-03-15; use the async v2 GA unbilled API.

App+User only. Response is a binary PDF (Content-Type application/pdf) - read it as bytes, not JSON.
Path is /documents/statement (singular). For Taiwan tax receipts use .../receipts/{receipt-id}/documents/statement.

country and segment are required; segment currently supports only 'commercial'.
Returns only currently-active promotions (by start/end dates). Covers NCE license-based promotions.
Supports both app-only and app+user.

country is required; promotion-id is a delimited product:sku:availability string - URL-encode it.
Returns the promotion ignoring start/end dates (works after expiry - useful for reconciliation).
Response may include promotionConstraints for eligibility checks. Supports both app-only and app+user.

country is required; 404 with error 400013 if not found.
A product is a grouping construct and is not itself purchasable - drill into SKUs/availabilities.
Supports both app-only and app+user.

country is required; 404 with error 400013 (product) or 400018 (SKU) if not found.
If purchasePrerequisites contains 'InventoryCheck' you must call Check Inventory before ordering.
Supports both app-only and app+user.

get.summary: Get a download link for the MCA template
get.description:
App+User only; public cloud + MCA only. Top-level /v1/agreementtemplates path (not under /customers).
country/language default to US/en-US; values are case-sensitive.
downloadUri (Word) and displayUri (preview) are freshly generated and EXPIRE after five minutes.

Supports both app-only and app+user (unlike update-customer-qualification, which is app+user only).
Returns an array; a customer can hold multiple (e.g. Education + StateOwnedEntity).
Values: Education, GovernmentCommunityCloud, StateOwnedEntity, Nonprofit, None; vetted types carry vettingStatus.

post.summary: Set a customer's qualification
post.description:
POST (not PUT); app+user only. Only Education, GovernmentCommunityCloud, StateOwnedEntity can be set.
Education requires educationSegment (K12 or HigherEducation); GCC requires a validationCode + a GDAP role.
Vetted types (Education/GCC) start in a review/vetting flow rather than immediately Approved.

post.summary: Check inventory for catalog items before ordering
post.description:
RETIRING 2026-09-25: migrate to the check-inventory-by-resource-type scenario, which adds a required resourceType filter.
Only needed for SKUs whose purchasePrerequisites contains 'InventoryCheck'; skip otherwise.
Required InventoryContext keys vary by SKU (declared in the SKU's inventoryVariables).
Items not found in the catalog are silently omitted from the result.
The docs accept app-only credentials here too, not only app+user.
For Azure RI purchases the azureSubscriptionId must already be registered and RI-enabled.

post.summary: Check inventory for catalog items filtered by resource type
post.description:
Replaces checkInventory, which retires 2026-09-25.
resourceType is a REQUIRED query parameter; the accepted values are in the resourceType enum (pc_get_enums).
A product missing from the response means unavailable for that subscription and region ONLY - do not read it as globally unavailable.
A SKU present with isRestricted true carries the reason in restrictions[] (e.g. reasonCode NotAvailableForSubscription).
Items not matching the requested resourceType are omitted, as are items absent from the catalog.
The docs accept app-only credentials here too, not only app+user.
For Azure RI purchases the azureSubscriptionId must already be registered and RI-enabled.

get.summary: Get a service request by ID
get.description:
App+User only. There is no REST endpoint to list support topics or to create a service request (portal-only).
Pass IncludeOrganizationRequests to read a request owned by the organization.

patch.summary: Update a service request (add note / close)
patch.description:
App+User only. Send only the fields you want to change.
Add notes via the singular NewNote object (the Notes array is read-only).

post.summary: Upload devices as a new batch (Autopilot)
post.description:
Returns 202 Accepted with a Location header (/customers/{id}/batchJobStatus/{tracking-id}) - poll it for status.
App+User only. Each device must satisfy one of the accepted id field combinations.
Add devices to an EXISTING batch via update-devices instead of reusing a batchId.

get.description:
Each batch item has a devicesLink to fetch that batch's devices.
Supports both app-only and app+user.

post.summary: Add devices to an existing batch
post.description:
Body is a bare JSON ARRAY of Device objects (unlike create-device-batch, which wraps them).
Returns 202 Accepted with a Location header to poll. Supports both app-only and app+user.

get.description:
The wire path is /policies (the SDK surface is named ConfigurationPolicies).
policySettings is an enum: remove_oem_preinstalls, oobe_user_not_local_admin, skip_express_settings, skip_oem_registration, skip_eula.
Supports both app-only and app+user.

get.summary: Get a reseller relationship request URL to send a customer
get.description:
A GET that returns a personalized { url } invitation link to send the customer; no request body.
App+User only. The customer accepts it in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
Not available for customer tenants with B2C/CIAM features enabled.

All query params optional. Base model: EventStatus, SubscriptionId.
With X-NewEventsModel: true you also get EventType, PageSize, PageNumber (both must be nonzero to page).
Microsoft is steering partners to the Graph partner security alerts API; this remains usable during transition.

get.summary: Get the Azure Partner Shared Services rate card
get.description:
The 'shared' variant for Azure Partner Shared Services; the standard one is /v1/ratecards/azure.
currency/region optional (default from the partner profile). All rates are pretax.

Note the /partner/v1/ path prefix (not /v1/). App+User only; CSP partners only.
OData params: top (max 10000), skip, filter, orderby, groupby, aggregationLevel (day|week|month).
Response includes a next link when more rows exist than 'top'.

post.summary: Assign a directory role to a customer user
post.description:
App+User only; requires the GDAP Privileged Role Administrator role.
role-id is the directory role's GUID (from the customer's directoryroles collection).
Returns 201 Created on success.

patch.description:
Use the dedicated /resetpassword sub-resource - NOT the generic update-user PATCH.
App+User only; needs the GDAP User Administrator (or Privileged Authentication Administrator) role.
Not supported in US Gov - use the Azure portal there.

Only within the 30-day window after deletion; after that the account is purged.
App+User only; needs GDAP User Administrator or Directory Writer.
Find the deleted user-id via the deleted (UserState=Inactive) users list.

delete.description:
Returns 204. The user state is set to inactive for 30 days, then purged and made unrecoverable; within that window restore-user (PATCH state=active) brings it back.
A deleted (inactive) user is no longer returned by get-customer-users. Remove licenses (assign-licenses licensesToRemove) and directory roles (remove-user-role) first for a clean offboarding.
App+User credentials only; needs the User Administrator GDAP role.

get.description:
App+User only. billingCurrency is fixed at account creation and cannot be changed.
Returns companyName, address, primaryContact, purchaseOrderNumber, taxId, billingCurrency, billingDay.

put.description:
PUT (full replace), not PATCH: GET it, mutate, then PUT the whole resource back.
App+User only. Modern 'G' invoices may not reflect PO-number changes made here (may need a support request).

get.summary: Get the partner legal business profile
get.description:
Path segment is 'legalbusiness' (one word).
Returns companyName, address, primaryContact, companyApproverAddress/Email, vettingStatus/vettingSubStatus.

App+User only. GET path is /v1/profiles/support but the UPDATE path is /v1/profiles/supportprofile - they differ.
Returns email, telephone, website.

App+User only. Update via PUT /v1/profiles/organization (full resource).
Returns id, companyName, defaultAddress, tenantId, domain, email, language, culture.

get.summary: Download an invoice receipt statement (Taiwan tax receipt)
get.description:
Taiwan tax receipts only - not a general invoice download. Response is a binary PDF (read as bytes).
App+User only. Needs both an invoice id and a receipt id (from the invoice's tax-receipt collection).

get.summary: Get a list of Azure entitlements for a subscription
get.description:
For an Azure plan, pass the Azure plan's subscription (plan) id as {subscription-id}; the response lists the underlying Azure usage subscriptions (azureEntitlementId values) created under it.
Each azureEntitlementId is what you use to cancel a single Azure subscription (POST .../azureEntitlements/{entitlement-id}) without cancelling the whole plan.
Also supports standalone App (app-only) credentials.

post.summary: Register a subscription for Azure reservations
post.description:
Registration is a prerequisite before purchasing Azure reservations (Reserved VM Instances) on a subscription.
No request body. Returns 202 Accepted with a Location header (.../registrationstatus) - poll it with get-subscription-registration-status until status is 'registered'.
For new commerce, register the Azure plan first: pass the Azure plan id as {subscription-id}.

get.description:
status is one of 'registered', 'registering', or 'notregistered'; poll after register-subscription until it reads 'registered'.
This is the URL returned in the Location header of register-subscription; you can call it directly with the same {subscription-id}.

get.summary: Get the signed-in partner's indirect resellers or providers
get.description:
relationship_type is required: use IsIndirectCloudSolutionProviderOf when signed in as an indirect provider (returns your resellers), or IsIndirectResellerOf when signed in as a reseller (returns your providers). See enum partnerRelationshipType.
App+User credentials only - this is a two-tier CSP (indirect) operation. Each item exposes the partner's mpnId, used as PartnerIdOnRecord when placing orders for a reseller's customer.
Only meaningful for indirect providers/resellers; direct-bill partners have no such relationships.

get.summary: Get the partners (indirect resellers/providers) of a customer
get.description:
Returns which partners have a reseller relationship with this customer; relationshipType reads e.g. is_indirect_cloud_solution_provider_of and each item carries the partner's mpnId.
App+User credentials only. Use this to confirm both you and your indirect provider hold a reseller relationship before transacting on the customer's behalf.
To establish a missing relationship, send the customer the invitation link from get-reseller-relationship-url.

get.summary: Get a customer's available licenses (subscribed SKUs)
get.description:
Step before assign-licenses: each SubscribedSku exposes productSku.id (the skuId you pass in licensesToAssign) plus availableUnits/consumedUnits so you can check seats before assigning.
App+User credentials only; needs a GDAP role such as Directory Reader, Global Reader, User Administrator, or License Administrator.
Returns the default license group's SKUs; a license can only be assigned to a user in the same group.

get.summary: Get the licenses assigned to a user
get.description:
Verifies what assign-licenses applied: each License lists its skuId and the assigned/excluded servicePlans.
App+User credentials only; needs a GDAP role such as Directory Reader, License Administrator, User Administrator, or Directory Writers.
Returns the default license group's assignments for the user.

delete.summary: Remove a customer user from a directory role
delete.description:
The inverse of assign-user-role; the response body is empty on success.
Part of offboarding: strip elevated directory roles before deleting the user.
App+User credentials only; needs the User Administrator GDAP role.

get.summary: Get the custom term end dates available for co-termination
get.description:
term_duration is required; supported values are P1M, P1Y and P3Y. term_start_date cannot be in the past.
The returned dates are the values you may pass as customTermEndDate when purchasing or scheduling - do not invent one.
Monthly (P1M) results cannot always be used for alignment: they do not work against a subscription ending on the 28th, 29th or 30th unless that is the last day of the month.
A maximum of 300 records comes back per page; continue with the token returned in the response header.

get.summary: Get the upgrades available for a legacy subscription
get.description:
This is the LEGACY upgrade path. New Commerce subscriptions use get-subscription-transition-eligibilities followed by create-subscription-transition instead.
The same page documents POST on the target subscription's /upgrades route to perform the upgrade; the GET only lists what is possible.
An empty list means no upgrade path exists for that offer - it is not an error.

get.summary: Get the paid offers a trial subscription can convert into
get.description:
Legacy trials only; a New Commerce trial converts through the transition API (get-subscription-transition-eligibilities + create-subscription-transition).
Each returned offer carries a default quantity equal to the trial's seat count - override it on the POST if the customer wants a different number.
The subscription id must be the TRIAL subscription.

post.summary: Convert a trial subscription to paid
post.description:
Take offerId and targetOfferId from get-trial-conversion-offers rather than composing them yourself.
Legacy trials only - New Commerce trials convert via create-subscription-transition.
Converting does not create a second subscription: the trial becomes the paid subscription, so the subscription id stays the same.

post.summary: Check eligibility for an Azure plan product upgrade
post.description:
A POST, not a GET, and it lives on the partner-wide /v1/productUpgrades route - the customer travels in the body, not the path.
Run it before create-azure-plan-upgrade; the response says why an upgrade is blocked.
This is the Azure-plan upgrade, unrelated to seat-based transitions.

post.summary: Get the status of a product upgrade
post.description:
A POST even though it only reads status, and it still needs the ProductUpgradeRequest body.
upgrade-id comes from the response of create-azure-plan-upgrade; an Azure plan upgrade is asynchronous, so poll here rather than assuming the POST finished the work.

get.summary: Get the add-ons bought against a subscription
get.description:
Returns the add-on subscriptions attached to this base subscription; each carries parentSubscriptionId pointing back at it.
Whether more add-ons can be bought is on the BASE subscription's hasPurchasableAddons field, not in this response.
Add-ons appear in list-customer-subscriptions too - filter on parentSubscriptionId to tell them apart from standalone subscriptions.

put.description:
PUT, not PATCH: the body replaces the cart, so omitting a line item removes it.
Carts expire - check expirationTimeStamp before updating an old one.
Only valid before checkout; after checkout-cart the purchase is an order and changes go through the order or subscription.

get.description:
A 2xx from checkout-cart or create-order means ACCEPTED, not provisioned. Poll here until status is success before telling a customer their licenses exist.
Status is reported per line item, so a partially provisioned order is normal - check every line item.
See the provisioningStatus enum for the values (success | pending | failed).

Use this to confirm that a write actually landed - a quantity change or cancellation is accepted asynchronously, so re-reading the subscription alone can show stale values.
It reports the provisioning of the subscription, not its lifecycle state; status on the Subscription resource is the lifecycle state.
Values are success | pending | failed (see the provisioningStatus enum).

get.summary: Get the activation link for an order line item
get.description:
Only products that require activation (Microsoft Marketplace SaaS and similar) return a link; an empty result for a seat-based offer is expected, not an error.
line-item-number is the LineItemNumber from the order, starting at 0 - it is not the subscription id.
The customer has to open the link to finish activation; the purchase is not usable until they do.

post.summary: Validate a legacy subscription for New Commerce migration
post.description:
Run this before every migrate-to-new-commerce; it returns isEligible plus the specific reasons a subscription cannot migrate.
It does NOT tell you whether the subscription is eligible for New Commerce promotions - that is a separate question.
Validating with termDuration/billingCycle set checks the migration you actually intend, not just the like-for-like one.

get.summary: Get a New Commerce migration by ID
get.description:
migration-id comes from the response of migrate-to-new-commerce; migration is asynchronous, so poll here instead of assuming the POST finished it.
The response carries the resulting New Commerce subscription id once the migration completes.
For the step-by-step trail (including failures) use get-migration-events.

get.summary: Query New Commerce migrations across customers
get.description:
Partner-wide route: there is no {customer-id} path segment, the customer travels as a query string.
At least one of CustomerTenantId, CurrentSubscriptionId or ExternalReferenceId is required; passing several is allowed.
ExternalReferenceId is the migration BATCH id - it is how you follow a bulk migration.
A maximum of 300 records comes back per page; continue with the token in the response header.

get.summary: Get the event trail of a New Commerce migration
get.description:
At least one of MigrationId or CurrentSubscriptionId is required.
This is the audit trail of what a migration actually did - the only way to see how far a migration got after the fact.
eventName values are in the migrationEventType enum; MigrationCompleted is the terminal one.

post.summary: Schedule a New Commerce migration for later
post.description:
Exactly one of targetDate or migrateOnRenewal drives the timing: set targetDate for a fixed date, or migrateOnRenewal true to run at the legacy renewal.
Scheduling does not validate later - run validate-migration first, because the schedule fails silently at run time if the subscription became ineligible.
addOnMigrations is a FLAT array of add-on subscriptions, each with its own term and billing cycle.

get.summary: Get a New Commerce migration schedule
get.description:
schedule-id is the id returned by create-migration-schedule, not the migration id.
The same page documents a partner-wide variant, GET /v1/migrations/newcommerce/schedules?CustomerTenantId={customer-id}, for listing every schedule.
A schedule that already ran is found through get-migration / get-migration-events, not here.

put.summary: Update a New Commerce migration schedule
put.description:
PUT, not PATCH: the body replaces the schedule, so send every field you want to keep.
Only a schedule that has not run yet can be updated; after it runs, the migration is a fact - see get-migration.
To stop a schedule entirely use cancel-migration-schedule.

post.summary: Cancel a New Commerce migration schedule
post.description:
A POST to a /cancel sub-route, NOT a DELETE on the schedule - sending DELETE returns 404.
Cancels the scheduled migration only; a migration that already ran cannot be undone this way.
Cancelling the schedule leaves the legacy subscription exactly as it was.

post.summary: Accept a transfer
post.description:
Called by the SOURCE partner on a transfer the target partner created with create-transfer / create-legacy-transfer.
Accepting is what actually moves billing ownership; poll get-transfer until the status leaves InProgress.
To decline instead use reject-transfer (a PATCH with status "reject").

get.description:
Support contact is per SUBSCRIPTION, not per customer - two subscriptions of one customer can be supported by different partners.
In indirect (two-tier) CSP this is how you tell whether the reseller or the provider owns support for a subscription.

put.description:
PUT, not PATCH - the body replaces the whole support contact.
The target partner must already have a relationship with the customer, otherwise the call is rejected.
Set per subscription, so moving support for a customer means iterating their subscriptions.

get.description:
Returns tenantId, companyName and the customer's primary domain - the domain is what you need when inviting users or checking a duplicate tenant.
get-customer-by-id returns the same profile nested; this route is for when you only want the company block.
The company profile is read-only through the API; the customer changes it in their own tenant.

Read this before update-customer-billing-profile: the write is a PUT of the whole profile and needs the ETag this response carries.
Holds the billing email, culture, language and default address - the address that address validation rules (get-country-validation-rules) apply to.
This is the CUSTOMER's billing profile; the partner's own is get-billing-profile.

put.description:
If-Match with the ETag from the GET is REQUIRED; without it, or with a stale one, the write fails with 2055.
PUT, not PATCH: the body replaces the profile, so send every field you want to keep.
Validate the address against the market's rules first (get-country-validation-rules, validate-address) - a rejected address blocks transacting.

get.description:
Organization-level tenant detail, distinct from the company profile returned by get-customer-company-profile.
Useful when reconciling a customer the partner did not create, where the company profile alone is ambiguous.

Lists the domains already added to the customer tenant - check here before creating users, because a user's UPN must use one of them.
The onmicrosoft.com default domain is on the company profile, not necessarily in this list.
To register another one use add-verified-domain; to check whether a domain is free use check-domain-availability.

post.summary: Add a verified domain to a customer
post.description:
This RECORDS a domain that is already verified; it does not perform DNS verification. Verify in the customer tenant first or the call is rejected.
Read the current list with get-customer-custom-domains before adding, to avoid a duplicate.
Adding a federated domain changes how the customer's users sign in - do not do it as a side effect of onboarding.

get.summary: Get a customer's account validation status
get.description:
App+User credentials only - an app-only token is rejected with 900329.
type=account is the documented validation type; the status is what decides whether the customer may transact at all.
A customer under review fails purchases with 800075 - check here before blaming the cart.

get.summary: Get the partner's Government Community Cloud validation codes
get.description:
US GOVERNMENT ONLY (Partner Center for Microsoft Cloud for US Government). A validation code is required to create a customer in the Government Community Cloud.
"all" is a literal path segment here, not a placeholder for a customer id.
Irrelevant in the commercial cloud - create-customer needs no validation code there.

get.summary: Get address formatting rules for a market
get.description:
The two-character ISO country code is the path segment - the market, not a language.
Tells you which address fields are required, whether a state/region list is fixed, and the postal-code format - drive your address form from this rather than hardcoding per country.
validate-address enforces these same rules; call this first if you want to fail in the UI rather than at the API.
